subject: math
title: 2 questions from earlier lessons
instructions: Work every problem on paper first and show each step. Then type your answer and press Check. You get two tries on each question. Type a fraction like 3/4, a mixed number like 2 1/2, and a power like 3^4.

skills.frac-mult-simplify: Simplify and cancel in fraction products

sections.name: Catch-up
sections.desc: Questions you missed before, with new numbers or a new story. Right on the first try takes one off your list.

items.q: A garden center needs help watering plants for 7 days while the owner is away, and it offers your family two ways to be paid. Plan A pays $95 every day. Plan B pays $5 on day 1, and the pay doubles every day after that: day 2 pays $10, day 3 pays $20, and so on.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Total pay for the 7 days under Plan A

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Pay on day 7 alone under Plan B

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Total pay for the 7 days under Plan B

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Which plan should your family take for these 7 days?

ans.model: Plan A pays $665 in total. Plan B pays $635 in total, so Plan A pays $30 more. Doubling starts small, and 7 days is not long enough for Plan B to catch up.
ans.look: Names both totals ($665 and $635) and says how much more Plan A pays ($30).

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Give the reason for your choice. Name both totals and say how much more the better plan pays.

a: b) Double each day: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320. Day 7 pays $320.
d) and e) Decision: Plan A, because $665 is more than $635.
items.hint: Write the day numbers 1 to 7 in a row and the pay under each one. Add the row twice to check the total before you decide.

items.q: Multiply 6/7 × 14/27. Write your answer in simplest form.
items.hint: Divide the top and the bottom by a common factor, then look again for another one. Before you check, read your answer back to be sure the fraction bar is there.
